1. Purpose. This article covers special situations not normally associated or considered with the
regular assignment process as outlined in references (a) through (g).
2. Definitions
a. Individual Ready Reserve (IRR). A force that consists of personnel who must fulfill their
military service obligation under 10 U.S.C., 651 and members fulfilling a service obligation
incurred via contract. The IRR is composed of the Active Status Pool (ASP) and the Voluntary
Training Unit (VTU) per reference (f).
b. IRR-ASP. A manpower pool consisting of individuals who are serving in a non-pay, non­
drill status per reference (f).
c. VTU. Unique to the Navy Reserve, VTUs are a subset of the IRR and consist of
personnel organized into units, who are not in a pay status, but who voluntarily drill for
retirement point credit.
3. Responsibilities
a. Navy Reserve Center (NRC) Commanding Officer (CO) will:
(1) Act as the reporting senior for the VTU, and is responsible for the continual screening
and management of the NRC's VTU. The CO may delegate this authority, in writing, in
accordance with reference (g).

(2) Determine the best use ofVTU Sailors to maximize the support of the Navy Reserve
and Supported Commands.
(3) Ensure Sailors transferring to the VTU receive counseling regarding their affected
benefits and incentives.
b. VTU Sailors will:
(1) Prior to transferring to the VTU, sign a NAVPERS 1070/613, Administrative
Remarks acknowledging their status change and subsequent affects on benefits and incentives
per reference (f).
(2) VTU Sailors must maintain satisfactory participation requirements per references (a)
and (b).
(a) VTU Sailors who fail to perform regularly scheduled Inactive Duty for Training
(IDT) periods are subject to the same policies as Sailors in a Selected Reserve (SELRES) status.
(b) Accumulation of more than the allocated unauthorized absences (UA) or
authorized absences (AA), per references (a) and (c), will result in transfer to the IRR-ASP or
administrative separation.
(c) VTU Sailors may perform Funeral Honors Duty (FHD) in accordance with
reference (c).
1- It is not the intention for Sailors assigned to the VTU to only perform FHD;
regular IDT participation is also required.
2. Sailors who are only interested in performing FHD may do so as members of
the IRR-ASP.
c. VTU Sailors may request Active Duty Training or Active Duty for Operational Support
orders if funding is available and appropriate training opportunities exist.
4. VTU Assignment Process
a. Personnel desiring transfer from IRR-ASP status to a VTU should contact their local
reserve recruiter for assistance.
b. COMNAVRESFORCOM (N12) assigns Sailors to a VTU attached to the NRC closest to
their residence.
(1) If the NRC is greater than 50 miles away, then berthing will be provided by the NRC.

(2) If the NRC is greater than 100 miles away, then the Sailor must sign a NAVPERS
1070/613, Administrative Remarks acknowledging that they freely accept commuting this distance
or the Sailor will be transferred to the IRR-ASP.
c. If the Sailor desires to be assigned to an alternate VTU, the Sailor must sign a NAVPERS
1070/613 Administrative Remarks acknowledging the NRC is greater than 50 miles away and
there is another NRC less than 50 miles away. The Sailor must acknowledge that berthing will
not be provided.
d. Request for transfers to the IRR must be submitted via the member's chain of command
no earlier than 90 days from the requested transfer date, via the NSIPS Retirements &
Separations module, with accompanying NAVPERS 1070/613s as required by references (d) and
(e).
